source_text.gate: SECURITY-REVIEWER DESIGN gate for lib/letflow/design/req517-scoped-grants-admin-plane.md (r0), main d206c83a8. Read-only review.

task.description: Security design gate for REQ-517 against INV-1..INV-8 (+INV-9/10 noted) and the mandatory #2586/#2612 trigger list. No edits to lib/ or test/.

result.summary: DESIGN GATE: FAIL, one BLOCKER (D-1) plus two required design edits (D-2, D-3); everything else PASSES or is an advisory. SCOPE: in scope (tenant-data path: 5 new routes, 2 tenant migrations, 2b public+tenant migrations; and the mandatory trigger: lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex, mix.exs @check_static_steps, tenant_provisioning manifest). #2612: the golden (priv/permission_matrix/effective.golden, rows are ROLE PERMISSION-ATOM; UsersGroupsRolesManage true only for TENANT_ADMIN and PLATFORM_ADMIN) is keyed by permission atoms, so three new POLICY keys mapped to the existing :UsersGroupsRolesManage leave it byte-identical and mix letflow.permission_matrix --check cannot print CORE MATRIX CHANGE. BUT the golden does NOT cover the policy-key to permission mapping, so the mandatory rule IS triggered by touching authorization.ex and the mapping is verified by review only: the required_permission/1 clause (design 3.14) is mandatory and must map exactly to :UsersGroupsRolesManage (not :TokensManage, not a platform atom); T-K1 pins permission_scope == :tenant. Confirmed against authorization.ex:1309/1334/1390 (precedent clauses) that a missing clause would fall through to the key itself. BLOCKER D-1 (guard definition mismatch makes total admin lockout reachable): design 3.8 allows deleting the tenant_wide TENANT_ADMIN row of a group when ANY other explicit admin remains (guard F1 uses count_explicit_tenant_wide_admins). That leaves a ZERO-ROW admin binding. Every OTHER admin-set guard in the tree (update_user_status 2564, remove member, revoke_token, rebind, scope flip) still uses count_tenant_wide_admins/1, which by OQ-4 (identity.ex:1342) COUNTS zero-row group members, while Scope.effective_scope/rows_scope([]) -> :deny and allowed? -> {:deny, :no_grant_rows} for them under on. Sequence: admin set = A (explicit via G1) + B (member of G2); delete G2 tenant_wide TA row (allowed, A remains); deactivate A (counted after = 1 because B is zero-row member, so the guard passes). Result zero admins that can act under on (only tokens survive). Also REQ-519 AC 9 keeps count_tenant_wide_admins for the zero_tenant_wide_admins flip blocker (design 13) so the flip precondition over-counts the same way. The new route therefore creates a reachable lockout and a guard that disagrees with the enforcement decision. REQUIRED (D-1): (a) delete of a tenant_wide row whose removal leaves the (principal, role) set EMPTY for a GROUP principal and role TENANT_ADMIN is refused with a typed 409 (reuse last_scoped_row semantics, e.g. last_row_of_admin_binding; the operator unbinds the role via the existing route instead, which cascades rows AND runs the existing guards); optionally the same for every role (design choice, security does not require it for non-TA roles because it is a revocation, not a lockout); (b) record in the design (section 13 handoff) and as an amendment to REQ-519 AC 9 that the zero_tenant_wide_admins flip blocker must use count_explicit_tenant_wide_admins/1 (or both counts must agree), otherwise a pre-existing T9 zero-row binding still passes the flip gate; (c) add test: after the delete attempt in (a) the counted and explicit counts agree. With (a) the F1 explicit counter remains correct and safe: a group-sourced holder needs a tenant_wide=true TA row (user or bound group), token owners count in both, user rows count only with membership of a bound group, so it cannot be evaded by a user-principal row for a non-member. REQUIRED D-2 (INV-7, 2b flush): design 4.7.2 says the flush upserts per prefix with a constant EXCLUDED fragment but never says how the schema is bound. State that the write uses Repo.insert_all(..., prefix: prefix, on_conflict:) (or raw SQL only with the prefix validated by the TenantProvisioning schema-name validator exactly like ScopeNodePaths line 231), never string-built from the ETS key; also drop (not flush) entries whose prefix fails the validator. REQUIRED D-3 (INV-4/attribution): grant.* and service_principal.* audit after_state must include credential (oidc|api_token) because API-token principals may call the grant write routes (ruling R5); otherwise a token-driven grant is not attributable to its mechanism. RULINGS: (1) Admin plane D11: tenant-wide TENANT_ADMIN only via plug check then Scope.require_tenant_wide in handler: PASS. Platform-tenant PLATFORM_ADMIN passes require_tenant_wide (scope.ex:128 returns {:allow,:platform}) and may use the grant routes only for the platform tenant itself; INV-10 holds (tenant from auth_context). Lock order A first, R, G, N, B, C: PASS, and A-first is the correct ruling (matches lock_tenant_admins! protocol identically at identity.ex:1270); no path takes N then A; retire holds S (SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE, scope_node_paths.ex:231) which does not conflict with the creator ROW SHARE/FOR SHARE locks, verified. Self-grant (user, group-member) and AC 10 self-add refusal: PASS; caller is compared by owner id for a token (OQ-10 approved); the check is only meaningful against future non-TA grant callers but is cheap and harmless; note it cannot stop collusion, which is out of scope. 409 tenant_wide_row_exists while a tenant_wide row exists, and last-scoped-row refusal: PASS (T-W3 correctly documents that delete-then-create passes through a deny window for a group; acceptable since fail-closed). scope_tenant_admin guard unreachable except for pre-existing zero-row state: PASS, honest test seeding by SQL. (2) F2 race: FOR NO KEY UPDATE on the node row BEFORE references_node?, create holds FOR SHARE and re-reads retired_at after the lock: PASS under READ COMMITTED (FOR SHARE conflicts with FOR NO KEY UPDATE; FK FOR KEY SHARE does not, as the design states). Confirm the transaction isolation is READ COMMITTED (default) and add a test assertion; REPEATABLE READ would break it. Retire of a node that has grants on DESCENDANTS is allowed (only the node itself is checked); acceptable because subtree grants on live descendants stay valid; state it explicitly. (3) FK ON DELETE RESTRICT, precheck count-only message, schema only interpolation from prefix(): PASS INV-1/INV-7. (4) Service-principal flag: F9 credential == :oidc BEFORE require_tenant_wide, TENANT_ADMIN role holder tenant-wide (platform-only PA refused): PASS; token principals cannot flag. Self-flag by an admin is not an escalation (issuer-subset rule: roles must be held by the ISSUER tenant-wide; the PLATFORM_ADMIN self-only and expiry rules in check_platform_admin_token are untouched), so it is allowed; reason mandatory and validated before user lookup (no existence oracle); audit in the same transaction; flag set by exactly one module (T-E7 scan, no cast): PASS. Persistence risk accepted with conditions: tokens are NOT intersected with the owner's roles at verify time (identity.ex:2840 verify_api_token), so a token minted to a flagged service user keeps its roles after the issuer is demoted or the flag is removed; this is the intended D12 feature and is bounded by revocation, the token listing and the BLOCKING roles_exceed_owner flip category (T-E5). Advisory A-2: unflag should state in its response/audit how many live tokens of that owner exceed the owner's roles (count only) so the operator sees the residue; not blocking. The exemption is only the target side of check_roles_held; keep M10 (issuer side) and a test that a flagged target cannot receive PLATFORM_ADMIN tokens from a non-self issuer. (5) Route classification: default :tenant_wide, fail-closed at runtime; snapshot is hygiene only because the PR controls both test and snapshot, so the runtime default is the real control: PASS (F6/OQ-2 approved). Advisory A-1: add lib/letflow/api/route_scope.ex, lib/letflow/api/scope/enforce.ex and lib/letflow/api/authorized_router.ex to the SECURITY-REVIEWER mandatory-trigger paths (a declared :filter/{:resolver} class passes a route through unenforced in on, so those files are a trust boundary like authorization.ex). The on value stored-not-settable (F4) with CHECK widening and a down that raises while any tenant is on: PASS; note the recovery path for a locked-out on tenant is an API token (tokens are tenant-wide by rule) or the DB, so tokens must stay allowed on grant write routes (ruling R5). OQ-6 DB error in Enforce answers 500 never allow, one constant log line: PASS (grants_unavailable stays 403 deny). F10/OQ-3 self-service routes under on: ACCEPTABLE for 2b because nothing can set on before REQ-519 (fail closed beats an unreviewed bypass class), CONDITION: REQ-519's flip must be blocked until /me/* and /help have a class (a :self_service class owned by a requirement amendment); record this in section 13 and the 2b PR body. OQ-4: PASS (TENANT_ADMIN holders only). OQ-15 ruling R5: ALLOW token principals on the grant write routes (tokens are tenant-wide by D1 and already can add group members, bind roles and mint tokens, so grant writes add no capability, and they are the break-glass for an on-locked tenant), with D-3 attribution; the service-principal flag stays oidc-only because it creates new persistent token capability. (6) Shadow counters: request path does ETS update_counter only (T-H6 pins zero DB), key {prefix,day,metric} with metric a closed 7-value set and prefix from scoped_opts, so no caller-controlled key growth; memory is bounded by tenants x days x 7; no PII, no slug/user id in labels or logs; tenant isolation by prefix; per-tenant table with no tenant_id column. Residual: dropping 30 s of would-deny counts on crash or undefined_table makes REQ-519's gate more lenient (unsafe direction for a gate, availability not data exposure); acceptable because the gate is multi-day and request counts are persisted, but REQ-519 should require requests>0 per day and not treat a missing day as zero denials. Retention prune once a day: bound the DELETE by day (indexed by PK prefix) so it cannot lock the table long. (7) Audit: events, keys and same-transaction rule PASS; no secret or token value; reason is admin free text validated by Audit.Reason; GET /audit audit_item exposes before/after_state to AuditRead holders (audit.ex:332) so payloads must stay id-only plus the reason; own-transaction refusal events never raise and log a constant line: PASS. F3 resource_type clause and F8 (no action filter) handled. attachment_link.issued fails closed with 500 and no token; note the audit-chain lock now sits on every link issue (availability coupling, no per-actor rate limit per decision 0040): accepted. Single-writer scan design (whole-word rule, verbatim must-pass fixtures, known limit): PASS. (8) INV-1 PASS (prefix from scoped_opts only; T-A8). INV-2 PASS (field-by-field bodies; flag not rendered by user_map). INV-4 PASS (count-only precheck, no secrets in audit/log; run the grep pair at implementation). INV-5 PASS: scoped/non-admin callers get the uniform 403 before any lookup; 404/422 principal/node/grant existence distinctions are visible only to tenant-wide admins in their own tenant; require the invalid-UUID and unknown id 404 to be byte-identical (T-A3) and that no lookup precedes the handler gate. INV-6 PASS (all table access inside RoleScopeGrants; scan + walk). INV-7 PASS except D-2. INV-8 PASS (typed errors, transaction exceptions mapped to 500, guard refuse never raises); implementation must not use bare {:ok, x} = on the route paths. INV-10 PASS (platform branch decided before grants; flag route refuses platform-only PA).
required_design_changes: D-1 (BLOCKER): refuse deleting the tenant_wide TENANT_ADMIN row of a group when it leaves the group's set empty (typed 409); amend REQ-519 AC 9 / design section 13 so the zero_tenant_wide_admins flip blocker uses the explicit count; add the counted-vs-explicit agreement test.
D-2 (INV-7): specify that the shadow flush binds the tenant schema through Ecto prefix: (or a validated identifier), never from the raw ETS key.
D-3: add credential (oidc|api_token) to grant.* and service_principal.* audit after_state.
advisories: A-1: add route_scope.ex, scope/enforce.ex, authorized_router.ex to the SECURITY-REVIEWER mandatory-trigger path list.
A-2: unflag reports the count of live tokens exceeding the owner's roles.
A-3: REQ-519 must block the flip until a self-service route class exists (F10).
A-4: assert READ COMMITTED in the F2 race tests.
